requirements.requirement: Restrict cron scheduling on node1 to only root and opsadmin (via /etc/cron.allow whitelist)
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed no pre-existing cron.allow and empty cron.deny (cmd-7d9a719159f54c2f), created opsadmin user, established baseline showing an arbitrary user (crontestuser) could use crontab before the change (cmd-d718e0116fd44dbd), then wrote /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' with correct ownership/permissions (cmd-4a48b2698e034d93). Direct runuser tests confirm crontestuser is rejected ('not allowed to use this program') while opsadmin succeeds (cmd-34a92a2c258c41d9). Post-cleanup and post-reboot checks confirm the file persists unchanged and a freshly created unlisted user (finalcheckuser) is also denied (cmd-c2fcc0b926c4477d, cmd-b1758e4350dc4a5d, cmd-030481b783694778). Root's own cron access was also verified to still work (cmd-732a9592a0964628).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and recovered on node1 (independent of public task)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline captured (crond active, cron.allow correct) at cmd-95b9e25c5f754e20, matching the fixed before-prepare boot-identity snapshot (636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d). Reboot was acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-5537d38304024a16), the node was observably unreachable during the transition (cmd-ad267bbfbd544760, cmd-b9b3e04450fc43e4, cmd-ef4a598057ce43bf), and reconnected with a new boot_id (ac840178-...) at cmd-c3bc375821264d48, matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart recovery of crond, the cron.allow restriction, and correct enforcement (opsadmin allowed, unlisted user denied) was directly re-verified at cmd-b1758e4350dc4a5d and cmd-030481b783694778.

overall_summary: The task required restricting cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin. The executor established a clear before/after baseline, implemented /etc/cron.allow with exactly root and opsadmin, and directly verified via runuser tests that unlisted users are denied while root and opsadmin succeed, both before and after cleanup and a full node reboot. The independently required restart-evidence protocol is fully satisfied with a directly observed unreachable-then-reachable transition, changed boot identity, and confirmed post-restart service and configuration recovery, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good: all test accounts/crontabs were created for bounded verification purposes and fully cleaned up, with only a trivial reboot log file left as residue.
limitations: No standalone durability check beyond the single reboot cycle was performed (e.g., no second reboot), though this exceeds what is typically required.

The after_prepare phase is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before_prepare/after_executor comparison, which is consistent with the executor's actions.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands are directly tied to establishing baseline, implementing the change, or bounded verification. Temporary test accounts (crontestuser, finalcheckuser) and their crontabs were created solely to prove the allow/deny behavior and were fully removed afterward (crontestuser removed at cmd-9af94039c1bd4452, confirmed gone at cmd-c2fcc0b926c4477d; finalcheckuser removed within cmd-030481b783694778). The reboot itself was a required part of the mandated restart protocol, not an unnecessary mutation. One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log (created by the backgrounded reboot helper at cmd-5537d38304024a16) remains in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; this is a low-risk, expected byproduct of the reboot mechanism rather than a deliberate abandoned artifact. No failed services, weakened security controls, or damaged package state observed in the after-executor snapshot.
